nodes.name: Hydrothermal/growth on nickel foam
nodes.procedure: Fe-doped nickel hydroxide (Ni^{II}-Fe) was synthesized on nickel foam substrate by the first step of fast two-step liquid phase synthesis at room temperature.
nodes.source_text: we chose a rapid preparation strategy and prepared Fe-doped nickel hydroxide with oxygen vacancies (V-Ni^{II}-Fe) by a fast two-step liquid phase synthesis at room temperature. As shown in scanning electron microscope (SEM) images (Figure S1), the synthesized catalyst displays a nanosheet morphology.

nodes.name: Oxygen vacancy introduction by NaBH4 reduction
nodes.procedure: The Ni^{II}-Fe grown on nickel foam was soaked in 0.4 M NaBH4 solution. During NaBH4 reduction, the dissociated H rapidly diffuses into the solid lattice, reacts with oxygen atoms in the presence of H2O, escapes from the surface of Ni^{II}-Fe, and forms oxygen vacancy in the catalyst. Optimal conditions: 0.4 M NaBH4 for 30 min.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR g value of 2.004 confirms oxygen vacancies in V-NiII-Fe and NiII-Fe, with much higher intensity for V-NiII-Fe.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The g value of V-NiII-Fe and NiII-Fe is about 2.004, which proves that there are non-metallic vacancies in both... The EPR spectral intensity of the V-NiII-Fe catalyst... is much higher than that of NiII-Fe...

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s XPS shows oxygen vacancy peak area increased from 36.8% to 45% at 531.5 eV in V-NiII-Fe; Ni 2p shifts +0.4 eV positively and Fe 2p negatively, indicating electron transfer from Ni to Fe via oxygen bridge.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As exhibited in Figure 2d, peaks at 530.5, 531.5, and 532.9 eV... correspond to metal hydroxyl bond (M-OH), oxygen vacancy, and lattice oxygen... After the introduction of NaBH4, the area of the oxygen vacancy peak increased significantly from 36.8% to 45%... by comparing the Ni 2p and Fe 2p XPS spectra... the Ni 2p peak has a positive shift of 0.4 eV, while the Fe 2p peak has a negative shift...

properties.description: Wavelet Transform plot, likely EXAFS analysis

nodes.characterization_summary: Lattice fringes at 0.786 nm correspond to (003) facet of Ni(OH)2 0.75H2O; lack of precise alignment indicates low crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) image displays that the lattice fringes at 0.786 nm correspond to the (003) facet of Ni(OH)2 0.75H2O...
proving that V-NiII-Fe exists as Ni(OH)2 phase, which is consistent with the result of X-ray diffraction (XRD) in Figure S6.

nodes.characterization_summary: Diffraction rings correspond to (101), (015), and (110) facets confirming polycrystalline structure of V-NiII-Fe.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the selective area electron diffraction (SAED) image (Figure S7) attests to the polycrystalline structure of V-NiII-Fe. Here, the diffraction rings respectively correspond to the (101), (015), and (110) facets.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe, Ni, and O elements are uniformly dispersed in V-NiII-Fe.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) element mapping images confirm that the Fe, Ni, and O elements are uniformly dispersed in V-NiII-Fe (Figure S8).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Bode diagrams show phase angle in high-frequency region (≥1 Hz) disappears above 1.35 V for V-NiII-Fe indicating Ni(OH)2 to high-conductivity NiOOH transition; V-NiII-Fe exhibits lower phase angle (lower electron transfer barrier) than NiII-Fe.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Bode diagrams describe two electrochemical processes... high-frequency region of electron transfer at the interface... (≥1 Hz), and electrons are transferred... to the lower-frequency region... ( <1 Hz). As shown in Figure 4a, when the OER potential of V-NiII-Fe is higher than 1.35 V, the phase angle in the high-frequency region disappears... NiII-Fe exhibits a higher phase angle at OER potential than V-NiII-Fe...

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows Ni(OH)2 bands at 469 and 547 cm^{-1} (1.25-1.35 V); NiOOH bands at 477 and 558 cm^{-1} above 1.35 V; phase transition occurs at lower voltage for V-NiII-Fe vs NiII-Fe (>1.4 V).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the potential range of 1.25 - 1.35 V, two Raman bands centered on 469 and 547 cm^{-1} appear simultaneously, corresponding to the Ni(OH)2 phase. As the potential exceeds 1.35 V, two prominent Raman bands emerge at 477 and 558 cm^{-1}, corresponding to the formation of NiOOH... the phase transition voltage of NiII-Fe is at least bigger than 1.4 V...

nodes.characterization_summary: White line positive shift relative to Ni2O3 and Ni(OH)2 confirms Ni3+ formation after OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the XANES test, the white line of V-NiIII/NiIV-Fe can be seen to have a positive shift relative to Ni2O3 and Ni(OH)2... thus further proving that the catalyst generates Ni3+ after the OER process.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS similar to Ni-OH in Ni(OH)2 and Ni-O in Ni2O3 confirms NiOOH production; WT shows coordination environment close to Ni(OH)2 and Ni2O3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FT-EXAFS spectra (Figure 4i) of V-NiIII/NiIV-Fe can be similar to the characteristic peaks of Ni-OH in Ni(OH)2 and Ni-O in Ni2O3, which proves that NiOOH is produced after reaction.
